title: "The Arrival of the Writer"
next_chapter_hook: The Writer of Fate spoke: "Chen Ji from ten thousand years ago, do you know why you have come?"

text.content: The complete form of the Tianji Record manifested in the world for the first time—not a gentle radiance, not a warm brilliance, but rather like ten thousand blades simultaneously unsheathing, illuminating the entire core of the Heavenly Realm as bright as day. Chen Ji floated at the very center of the radiance, his consciousness slowly rising from the abyss of a thousand-year slumber, like a fish leaping from the dark depths of the sea into the light. Every sense was relearning the laws of this world.

"Finally awake." A voice rang in his mind, belonging to no one he recognized—not Mo Xiansheng's aged tones, nor the childlike clarity of the Heaven's Eye, but something far more ancient and profound, as if the eternal night itself were speaking. Chen Ji opened his eyes to find himself floating in an endless white void, no earth beneath his feet, no stars above, only the complete Tianji Record radiating dazzling golden light suspended before him.

dialogue.content: "A thousand years of planning, and finally we have reached this point." The voice spoke again, carrying an indescribable pressure. "Chen Ji, do you know why you can see the future?"

text.content: Chen Ji felt the power surging within him—the Heavenly Fate Value accumulated by the Tianji Record during his thousand-year slumber—exactly 36,000 points, dozens of times what he had consumed in the past. What shocked him even more was that the Heaven's Eye originally residing in his Brow Center now floated at his right side, transformed into a young phantom with features similar to his own yet far more cold and severe. The gazes of the two met in the void.

The Heaven's Eye—or rather, the former Heaven's Eye—nodded slightly toward him. Those eyes no longer held a child's innocence, replaced instead by a kind of understanding and resolution tempered by the vicissitudes of countless years. "A thousand years of coexistence, today we part. From this moment, I am the Heaven's Eye, and you are you. The only bond between us is the Tianji Record itself."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stared at the Heaven's Eye's phantom, the corner of his lips slightly raised. That smile carried a touch of sarcasm and also a kind of relief: "As if I wanted to be bound to you. However—" He paused, his tone suddenly turning cold. "Before I figure out exactly what you are, you'd better not let me see you messing around inside the Tianji Record."

text.content: Before the words even finished, a crack suddenly appeared in the depths of the Void. Initially only the thickness of a hair, it expanded in the blink of an eye into a chasm stretching across ten thousand miles. Within the abyss, an eye slowly opened—that eye was impossibly vast, its pupil pure black, its iris burning with golden-red flames. Simply being gazed upon caused Chen Ji to feel waves of agony emanating from the depths of his soul.

dialogue.content: "Ten thousand years ago, you asked me the same question." The voice came from the abyss, shaking the entire Void. "I told you to come back after gathering the Tianji Record. Now—the time has come."

text.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes—thousand years of slumber had not dulled his thoughts, but instead elevated his computational abilities to an entirely new peak. Looking at that enormous eye burning with golden-red flames, countless possibilities flashed through his mind in an instant. This entity—the Writer of Fate—just what is it? Friend or foe? What does its mention of "ten thousand years ago" mean? Could it be that his past life, Chen Ji's former incarnation, had actually contacted the Heavenly Way itself?

choice.prompt: Facing the pressure of the Writer of Fate, Chen Ji had to make a choice. The thousand-year plan had reached its end, truth was within reach, yet danger lurked on all sides.

choices.description: "Taking the posture of a thousand-year planner to face it head-on, unafraid of any truth. Since we've come this far, there is no reason to retreat."
choices.visible_reward: "Gaining full recognition from the Writer of Fate"
choices.risk_hint: "The truth may subvert all his understanding"

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, fully mobilizing the 36,000 points of Heavenly Fate within him. Golden radiance exploded from his entire body, standing in distant opposition to the Writer of Fate's golden-red flames. Step by step, he walked toward the abyss, his voice cold as eternal glacial ice: "What I asked ten thousand years ago, I no longer remember. But right now—I still stand here. If you have something to say, speak freely."

dialogue.content: "Bold spirit." A note of what seemed like appreciation appeared in the Writer of Fate's voice. "Worthy indeed of one who could gather the Tianji Record. But before I reveal the truth, you must first pass the final test—prove you have the qualification to bear all of this."

choices.description: "Avoiding direct confrontation, first probing the other's cards and intentions. Thousand years of planning have made him accustomed to strategizing before acting."
choices.visible_cost: "May appear overly cautious and lose the initiative"
choices.visible_reward: "Obtaining more intelligence about the Writer of Fate"
choices.risk_hint: "The other party may see through the probe and disdain to respond"

text.content: Chen Ji did not rashly advance, but instead stood with hands clasped behind his back, his gaze sweeping repeatedly over that burning eye. His voice was unhurried, carrying a note of playful amusement: "What happened ten thousand years ago, I truly don't remember. But since you mention it, perhaps you wish to help me recall? Why not first explain what this 'test' of yours entails, so I don't fall into some trap blindly."

dialogue.content: That massive eye blinked, as if smiling: "You are indeed prudent. However——" The voice suddenly turned cold, "The master of the Tianji Record requires no testing. Testing is disrespectful to the Heavenly Dao."

choices.description: Preserve trump cards, avoid direct confrontation with this transcendent existence for now. Observe the situation first, seek an escape route.
choices.visible_cost: May be seen as cowardice, lose the interest of the Fate Writer
choices.visible_reward: Preserve oneself, retain room for maneuvering with other forces
choices.risk_hint: The Fate Writer may not permit anyone to escape

text.content: Chen Ji's footsteps paused slightly, his gaze flickering. He truly wasn't ready——a thousand years of slumber had indeed enhanced his power, but it had also disrupted his strategic rhythm to some extent. He stepped back, voice calm yet carrying a hint of retreat: "Since this is a test, surely you should give me some time to prepare. I've already gathered the Tianji Record, so why the urgency?"

dialogue.content: The eye in the abyss suddenly contracted into a thin line, golden-red flames nearly bursting forth: "Do you think you still have a choice?" The pressure crushed down like mountain and cliff toppling, the entire Void trembling beneath this force, "The day the Tianji Record is complete is when the test begins——this is not a request, it is the law of the Heavenly Dao!"

text.content: Beneath the pressure, Chen Ji's robes fluttered wildly, but his figure stood as steady as bedrock. The 36,000 Heavenly Fate points circulated within him, transforming into golden halos protecting his entire body. He gazed at that burning eye, his mind racing in calculation——though this pressure was strong, it was not unendurable. If the Fate Writer truly wanted to kill him, why speak at all? It wanted something else.

Just then, the Heaven's Eye phantom suddenly moved. It drifted before Chen Ji, facing that massive eye in the abyss, voice cold as the nine-yin cold spring: "Why must you frighten people? I don't know the details of your agreement with him ten thousand years ago, but I know he reached today through no stroke of luck. Rather than releasing pressure here——" It paused, a cold smile curling at its lips, "Why not tell him the truth."

dialogue.content: "The truth?" That massive eye slowly turned toward the Heaven's Eye, and its voice carried an unexpected complex emotion, "You are merely a wisp of obsession separated from him, yet dare speak such words to me?" It paused, then continued, "Very well. Since the Tianji Record is complete, telling him is without harm——Chen Ji, do you know what your name means?"

text.content: Chen Ji furrowed his brow. "Chen Ji"——this name was inherent to him since birth, and no one had ever told him there was any profound meaning. His father was merely an ordinary mortal, and his mother had vanished during his childhood. He had always believed it was just an ordinary name, nothing more——could there be some secret hidden within?

choice.prompt: The Fate Writer's question directly pointed to the mystery of Chen Ji's origins, the only territory his thousand-year scheme had never touched.

choices.description: Stop concealing, ask the question directly and straightforwardly. Chen Ji has never been someone who beats around the bush. Since the other party is willing to speak, he wants to hear it clearly.
choices.visible_cost: May lose composure before the truth
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information regarding one's own origins
choices.risk_hint: The truth may be diametrically opposed to his understanding

text.content: Chen Ji stepped forward, his gaze sharp as a blade, piercing directly into that burning massive eye: "What's wrong with my name, Chen Ji? Whatever it may be, please speak clearly. I didn't know a thousand years ago, but today after a thousand years, I believe I'm strong enough——strong enough to bear any answer."

dialogue.content: That massive eye fell silent for a moment, the golden-red flames burning more intensely. Finally, it spoke, voice like an ancient deity murmuring: "Chen Ji——'Chen' is the 'one' among the forty-nine derivations of Heaven, the one that slips away. 'Ji' is the 'variable' in Heaven and Earth's chess game. Ten thousand years ago, I personally sent you into reincarnation, making you forget everything, solely to wait for this day."

choices.description: Not directly asking the meaning of the name, but rather what exactly happened ten thousand years ago. He needs more information to judge truth from falsehood.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the opportunity to learn the truth directly
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more clues from the other party's response
choices.risk_hint: The Fate Writer may become impatient answering peripheral questions

text.content: Chen Ji did not rush to question the meaning of the name. Instead, he stood with hands clasped behind his back, his gaze deep and profound: "Ten thousand years ago, you cast me into the cycle of reincarnation? It sounds as though we have history. But what I am more curious about is—what happened back then? What made you, this 'Scribe of Fate,' personally arrange the fate of a mortal?"

dialogue.content: The flames in that giant eye flickered a few times, and a hint of nostalgia entered the voice: "Because you were the only one who could see through me. Ten thousand years ago, you—your true self—saw the end of Heavenly Dao, saw the secret I refuse to let anyone know. So, I had to make you forget."

text.content: Upon hearing the words 'the end of Heavenly Dao,' Chen Ji's heart sank heavily. The end of Heavenly Dao—what did that mean? Did it mean Heaven's Law was not eternal? Did it mean the operation of this world had its end point? And his past life ten thousand years ago had actually seen all this? He looked at the Heavenly Eye hovering beside him, its expression grave, clearly also digesting this shocking revelation.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then he smiled. That smile carried a hint of self-mockery, a hint of sharpness: "I saw something you didn't want anyone to see, so you threw me into reincarnation and erased my memory? Scribe of Fate, your memory isn't very good—aren't you afraid I'll remember that secret again this time?"

text.content: That giant eye fell silent again. This silence was even longer than before, the golden-red flames flickering more violently, as if brewing something. Finally, it spoke, its voice carrying a complex emotion Chen Ji could not comprehend: "So this is the 'test' I mentioned. The Chen Ji of ten thousand years ago chose death to preserve that secret, and this life—" The flames surged violently, "I want to see what choice you will make."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Death? His past life ten thousand years ago had chosen death to preserve the secret? What secret was so important that he would rather give up his life? And did the Scribe of Fate's 'test' mean forcing him to choose between preserving the secret and continuing to live? His gaze fell upon the complete Tianji Record floating beside him, golden light gently enveloping him, as if silently asking: What is your choice?

Just then, another tremor came from the depths of the Void. This tremor was different from before, carrying a strange sensation of temporal distortion. Chen Ji looked up to see a blurred figure slowly walking toward him from the distance. With each step the figure took, the surrounding time and space twisted, as if he himself was the incarnation of time itself. When the figure drew near, Chen Ji finally saw his face—it was a face almost identical to Chen Ji's own, only more aged, more exhausted, with eyes that glowed even more deeply. "I have been waiting for you for a long time," the figure spoke, its voice hoarse yet carrying endless vicissitudes, "My self of this era."
